question: Which way military_access the condition reads.

addresses.name: CGrantsMilitaryAccessTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`military_access = TAG`: `us->diplomacy (+0xE28) [other.id] ->hasMilitaryAccess (+0x4C) != 0`.** 0x5F7820 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F7891.

    THIS is EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40) - this_scope's country, or the owner of this_scope's province when it has none; FROM is `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country (+0x18/+0x1C)`; otherwise the tag at +0x40/+0x44 (CTagTrigger's). 

Direction: **the scope's country may pass through TAG's land** - not that it grants TAG access, which this entry said until 2026-10-13 on the strength of the class name. The byte is the one CMilitaryAccessAction::Apply sets for the asker on accepting (`SetMilitaryAccess(1, actor->diplomacy[recipient])` at 0xA23998, `confirmed` in FINDINGS-agreements.md, C.4) and CGrantMilitaryAccessEffect::Execute sets on the scope's status towards TAG; GRANT_MILITARY_ACCESS_EFFECT reads 'TAG will grant COUNTRY military access'. The class name describes TAG's side of it.
addresses.evidence: Direction settled by the access action's write at 0xA23998 (FINDINGS-agreements.md, C.4), which sets the same byte for the country that asked.
addresses.revises: Comment only: the direction was 'the scope grants TAG access', inferred from the class name; the access action's accepted arm sets this byte for the asker, so it is 'the scope may pass through TAG'.

slots_noted: CGrantsMilitaryAccessTrigger's slot is already named Evaluate in the record; this fragment revises the entry's comment only and leaves the slot as it is.
